title: Chalmers Next Labs, ConScience, and NQFF Validate Superconducting Qubit Chip Stability Across International Testbeds - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Chalmers Next Labs, ConScience and Singapore's NQFF shipped ConScience's QiB1 5-qubit superconducting processor from Gothenburg to Singapore and back during 2026, finding control frequencies stayed within 1% of baseline and T1 coherence remained above 100 μs. The partners are commercializing the Gothenburg–Singapore Twin Testbed as a standardized cross-facility measurement service for quantum component suppliers.

insights.claim: A joint study by Chalmers Next Labs, ConScience and Singapore's NQFF found that superconducting quantum processors keep stable physical performance when transported between international research facilities.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Reduces a practical risk in shipping and qualifying superconducting quantum hardware across borders.
insights.quote: superconducting quantum processors maintain stable physical performance characteristics when transported between international research facilities
insights.locator: In a joint hardware benchmarking study

insights.claim: After shipment from Gothenburg to Singapore and 80 hours of continuous automated testing, the ConScience QiB1 5-qubit processor's control microwave frequencies matched the original Gothenburg values within a <1% deviation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantifies how little calibration drift transit introduced, a key metric for distributed QPU testing and supply.
insights.quote: Control microwave frequencies matched initial Gothenburg values within a < 1% deviation margin.

insights.claim: When the QiB1 chip returned to Gothenburg in August 2026, its frequency remained within 1% of the January 2026 baseline and T1 coherence times stayed above 100 μs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows long-term (roughly seven-month) stability of a commercially fabricated superconducting chip after round-trip shipping.
insights.quote: Confirmed long-term frequency stability remained within 1% of January baseline; T1 coherence preserved > 100 μs.

insights.claim: Superconducting qubits depend on nanometer-thin aluminum oxide Josephson junctions, so their microwave operating frequencies are sensitive to fabrication variances, shipping stress and regional magnetic field differences.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Explains why transport robustness is a non-trivial hurdle for superconducting quantum hardware supply chains.
insights.quote: Superconducting qubits rely on nanometer-thin aluminum oxide Josephson junctions, making their microwave operating frequencies sensitive to fabrication variances, physical shipping stress, and ambient magnetic field differences

insights.claim: The WACQT–NQFF Twin Testbed study was funded by Swedish innovation agency Vinnova under the QUASI (Quantum Advancement through Sweden–Singapore Integration) framework.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Signals public funding backing bilateral quantum infrastructure between Sweden and Singapore.
insights.locator: Executed under the WACQT–NQFF Twin Testbed

insights.claim: The testbed collaboration puts into practice an October 2025 Memorandum of Understanding between Singapore's National Quantum Office (NQO) and the Quantum Sweden Innovation Platform (QSIP).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows government-level quantum partnerships translating into concrete technical programs.

insights.claim: Chalmers Next Labs and NQFF are commercializing the Gothenburg–Singapore Twin Testbed as a standardized cross-facility measurement service for quantum component suppliers, with full measurement data to be presented at the APS March Meeting 2027.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A new benchmarking-as-a-service offering could become part of quantum supply-chain qualification; watch the APS 2027 data release.
insights.quote: commercializing the Gothenburg–Singapore Twin Testbed as a standardized cross-facility measurement service for quantum component suppliers
